Owned by Jeff Bezos

1994: "Founded in 1994 by Jeff Bezos in Bellevue, Washington, the company started as an online book marketplace that gradually expanded to include virtually all consumer products as well as many other categories, positioned as "The Everything Store"." (source))
2026: "As of 2026 it was the world's biggest online retailer." (source))

2023: "As of 2023, it was the largest online retailer and marketplace, smart speaker provider, cloud computing service provider through AWS, live-streaming service provider through Twitch, and Internet company as measured by revenue and market share." (source))
2021: "In 2021, it surpassed Walmart as the world's largest retailer outside of China, supported by its subscription plan, Amazon Prime, which had 200 million subscribers worldwide." (source))

1994: "In November 1994, Bezos renamed the company Amazon to reflect his ambitions for his company. (Amazon is the world's largest river.) On July 16, 1995, the Amazon website launched, initially sourcing its books directly from wholesalers and publishers." (source#1994%E2%80%932010))
2015: "Annapurna Labs, an Israel-based microelectronics company reputedly for US$350–370M, acquired by Amazon Web Services in January 2015 ." (source#Other))
2018: "It was acquired in 2018 for under $1 billion." (source#Other))
2019: "Eero was acquired by Amazon in 2019 for US$97 million." (source#Other))
2019: "It was acquired in October 2019 to become part of Amazon Care." (source#Other))
2026: "In August 2026, Amazon announced that AWS Mechanical Turk would be discontinued on September 30, 2026, ending the service after more than 21 years." (source#2021%E2%80%93present))

"Amazon invested $475 million into Saks' acquisition of Neiman Marcus, and worried that Saks' bankruptcy would harm creditors and push the tech company further down the repayment pecking order." (source#2021%E2%80%93present))

"Amazon sells many products under its own brand names, including phone chargers, batteries, and diaper wipes. and features hundreds of product lines." (source#Private-label_products))
"Amazon owned 34 private-label brands as of 2019." (source#Private-label_products))
"These brands account for 0.15% of Amazon's global sales, whereas the average for other large retailers is 18%." (source#Private-label_products))
"Amazon allows users to submit reviews of each product." (source#Product_reviews))
"Reviewers rate the product from one to five stars and offer commentary." (source#Product_reviews))

"Amazon provides a badging option for reviewers that indicates the real name of the reviewer (based on confirmation of a credit card account) or that indicates that the reviewer is one of the top reviewers by popularity." (source#Product_reviews))
